newsitem.title: TURKEY: Afghan warlord Dostum says he will be missed.
newsitem.headline: Afghan warlord Dostum says he will be missed.

text.p: Ousted Afghan warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum said on Tuesday he would be missed by his ethnic Uzbek people now that radical Islamist Taleban forces had captured his stronghold, Turkey's Anatolian news agency reported.
"They will miss Dostum so much. The Jumbish-i Milli party was a source of hope for the Turkic people in Afghanistan," the agency quoted Dostum as saying.
Dostum arrived in the Turkish capital on Sunday after his headquarters in the northern Afghan town of Mazar-i-Sharif fell to his former commander General Abdul Malik in a mutiny.
The Taleban later took control of Mazar-i-Sharif in alliance with Malik and now control more than 90 percent of the country.
Dostum, a former pro-communist Uzbek chief, became the leader of the Jumbish-i Milli movement based in northern Afghanistan following his key role in the collapse of the communist government in 1992.
Turkey, along with Uzbekistan, was widely reported to have supported Dostum. Turks and Uzbeks share ethnic and linguistic links.
"It was not easy to establish Jumbish-i Milli which I lead. We have had 500,000 martyrs until coming to this stage, " Dostum said.
Dostum said his troops were fighting Taleban forces in three separate Afghan cities and he was in regular telephone contact with them.
Turkey said on Monday the ousted general could stay in the country as long as he wanted. Dostum has said he did not seek political asylum in Turkey and came for health reasons.
